name: @kobai/plugin-stripe
description: Stripe as a Plugin: PaymentIntents with automatic_payment_methods, and its own account of every payment it gave back for an Order that never existed.
// publishConfig: Published for the same reason as @kobai/core, and guarded the same way — a generated Project installs this Plugin as an ordinary dependency, so it has to exist in a registry (ADR-0034). `registry` pins publishing at a loopback address so reaching npmjs.com has to be deliberate rather than accidental. tests/publish-guard.test.ts fails the build if this pin goes missing.

scripts.// db:push: There is deliberately no db:push script here either — the rule is the same for every Plugin, and a Plugin is where it bites hardest. `drizzle-kit push` diffs a schema against the LIVE database, so pushing this Plugin's schema at a Project's database reports success while silently dropping Core's tables and every other Plugin's, leaving their tracking rows behind so the migration runner believes the work is done and cannot repair it. Observed, not theorised: FINDINGS.md section E on branch prototype/drizzle-multi-migration, and docs/adr/0030-generate-and-migrate-only-never-drizzle-kit-push.md. `tablesFilter` mitigates it and is set in drizzle.config.ts anyway, but the primary control is that the dangerous command is never available.

// dependencies: There is deliberately no `stripe` SDK here. This Plugin speaks to three of Stripe's REST endpoints over `fetch`, which is what lets `devbox run ci` replace the whole of the network with one option — and what keeps an SDK with its own Node expectations out of a Project's dependency tree for the sake of three calls.
